reason: Phagocytes are shown clearing debris near the cut, a useful early repair task.
expectation: The wound should be cleared of some debris while the vessel remains sealed.

effect: Phagocytes cleared debris and revealed three repair slots: supply, surface and support.
reaction: The separate slots make the remaining wound-repair tasks clearer.
reason: Repair signals are shown acting on the nearby capillary, suggesting a way to develop the wound's blood supply.
expectation: The signals should stimulate a vessel response that helps supply the wound.

effect: The repair signals produced a capillary sprout connected to the existing circulation, suggesting it can fill the supply slot.
reaction: The connection to the parent vessel makes the new supply route clear.
reason: The capillary sprout looks suited to the wound's empty Supply slot.
expectation: The sprout should provide a blood supply to the healing wound.

effect: The sprout filled the supply slot and formed a connected blood-flow route through the wound.
reaction: The completed loop makes the nutrient supply more convincing.
reason: The fibroblast picture shows a collagen gene, and RNA building blocks should let the cell begin making its message.
expectation: The fibroblasts should produce RNA for collagen synthesis.

effect: The fibroblasts now have collagen messenger RNA ready for ribosomes.
reaction: The DNA-to-RNA step clearly connects gene expression to repair.
reason: Matrix nutrients include amino acids needed to make collagen from the RNA instructions.
expectation: The fibroblasts should make collagen-containing support material for the wound.

effect: The fibroblasts used the nutrients to make and export collagen, forming new connective tissue for wound support.
reaction: The sequence connects the RNA message to collagen deposited outside the cell.
reason: The new connective tissue fits the wound's remaining Support slot.
expectation: The connective tissue should support the healing wound.

effect: The new connective tissue filled the support slot; the surface still needs repair.
reaction: The note that young tissue remains weaker makes the repair less instantaneous.
reason: Epidermal edge cells and their nutrients are the visible pieces for rebuilding the wound surface.
expectation: The cells should grow or spread to form a new surface over the wound.

effect: The edge cells formed a new epidermal sheet that can fill the remaining surface slot.
reaction: The sheet extending across the gap makes surface closure clear.
reason: The new surface fits the wound's remaining Surface slot.
expectation: The new epidermal sheet should close the wound surface.

effect: The new surface completed the wound's closure, support and supply goal; clearing the temporary clot remains.
reaction: The distinction between surface closure and deeper strengthening is useful.
reason: Clot-clearing enzymes are the remaining visible means of removing the temporary fibrin clot.
expectation: The enzymes should break down the temporary fibrin clot as healing proceeds.

effect: The enzymes cleared most temporary fibrin, completing both goals; the scar and its collagen continue to mature.
reaction: The still-maturing scar makes the ending feel more realistic than an instant return to uninjured skin.

mostWorthwhile.text: Making collagen instructions and then connective tissue was most worthwhile: the planned cutaways link DNA, messenger RNA, protein production and collagen export to wound repair.

leastWorthwhile.text: Fitting each finished component into the healing body was clear but somewhat repetitive after making it; the surface fitting added little beyond confirming closure.

surprise.text: The capillary sprout joined another vessel to form a flow route, rather than merely ending in the wound. The distinction between a closed surface and deeper tissue still gaining strength also stood out.

arbitrary.text: Nothing felt purposeless, though combining nutrients directly with edge cells to produce a complete new surface simplified the intervening repair process.

continue.text: Yes. I would be interested in another chapter that connects familiar cell biology to a larger bodily process as this repair sequence did, although the repeated fitting steps were less engaging.
